cipher.name: Base32HexAlphabetSubstitution
cipher.idea: To maximize the model's reasoning capability and ensure perfect implementation correctness, we use a simple, deterministic character-to-character substitution based on the standard Base32Hex alphabet (0-9, A-V). We map the 22 letters from A to V to their corresponding index characters in the Base32Hex alphabet, and map the remaining letters W, X, Y, Z to specific punctuation marks. Case is preserved by applying the same mapping to lowercase letters using lowercase outputs. Digits, spaces, and standard punctuation remain completely unchanged.
cipher.encrypt_rules: Each letter is substituted individually. The mapping for uppercase letters is: A->0, B->1, C->2, D->3, E->4, F->5, G->6, H->7, I->8, J->9, K->A, L->B, M->C, N->D, O->E, P->F, Q->G, R->H, S->I, T->J, U->K, V->L, W->M, X->N, Y->O, Z->P. Lowercase letters follow the exact same mapping but in lowercase: a->0, b->1, c->2, d->3, e->4, f->5, g->6, h->7, i->8, j->9, k->a, l->b, m->c, n->d, o->e, p->f, q->g, r->h, s->i, t->j, u->k, v->l, w->m, x->n, y->o, z->p. Digits, spaces, and punctuation marks are not changed.
cipher.decrypt_rules: Each character is substituted back to its original letter. The mapping for uppercase characters is: 0->A, 1->B, 2->C, 3->D, 4->E, 5->F, 6->G, 7->H, 8->I, 9->J, A->K, B->L, C->M, D->N, E->O, F->P, G->Q, H->R, I->S, J->T, K->U, L->V, M->W, N->X, O->Y, P->Z. Lowercase characters follow the exact same mapping but in lowercase: 0->a, 1->b, 2->c, 3->d, 4->e, 5->f, 6->g, 7->h, 8->i, 9->j, a->k, b->l, c->m, d->n, e->o, f->p, g->q, h->r, i->s, j->t, k->u, l->v, m->w, n->x, o->y, p->z. Digits that were originally part of the plaintext, spaces, and punctuation marks are not changed.

example.plaintext: The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.
